dek: Text Your Ex Back offers a multimedia texting system from an established relationship publisher. Hook Your Ex packages a newer set of named message templates around hypnosis-influenced techniques. The useful difference is teaching style and package depth—not a promise that either can make an ex return.
description: Compare Text Your Ex Back and Hook Your Ex by format, package transparency, checkout terms, practical fit, and relationship-safety limitations.

faqs.answer: Text Your Ex Back is the larger package, with an ebook plus video and audio training modules. Hook Your Ex is positioned as a compact course built around message templates.
faqs.question: Which program has more material?

faqs.answer: Both offer text versions of their presentations. Text Your Ex Back includes an ebook as part of its core package, while Hook Your Ex publishes a full text version of its pitch.
faqs.question: Which is better for someone who prefers reading?

faqs.answer: Neither product's core offer was presented as a subscription when reviewed, but always recheck the current order form for preselected upsells or recurring offers before paying.
faqs.question: Do either of these products include recurring charges?

faqs.answer: No. A messaging guide can organize ideas and examples, but it cannot control another person's feelings, consent, boundaries, or decisions.

verdict: Start with Text Your Ex Back when you want a structured multi-format program with separate guidance tracks. Choose Hook Your Ex when you want a compact set of ready-to-adapt message templates. Pause on both if the appeal depends on guaranteed reconciliation: no set of texts can override another person's boundaries or decisions.
